page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7t.large is an entry-level compute instance belonging to the Enhanced family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core via hyperthreading (2 threads per core). It includes 8.0 GB of memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The host platform runs on a KVM hypervisor with CPU instruction support including AVX, AVX-512 (Foundation and VNNI), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance provides 2 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and includes zero dedicated GPUs or bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread capabilities paired with constrained aggregate multi-threaded throughput. Single-core evaluations, including stress-ng (1855.08) and Geekbench (1553.0), demonstrate average performance within the broader cloud ecosystem. Common single-threaded utilities show reasonable capability, such as gzip compression at 28.03 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 10.82 GB/sec. However, because the instance relies on only two hyperthreaded vCPUs on a single core, multi-core benchmarks show sharp throughput constraints. Stress-ng multi-core testing reached 1896.44 and Geekbench multi-core measured 1808.0, placing both in the lower tiers. Workloads relying on multi-threaded execution like Clang software compilation (2118.0) and ray tracing (2244.0) reflect these hardware limits.

Memory-intensive and I/O-heavy operations show lower efficiency profiles due to narrow execution channels and restricted memory bandwidth. Uncached large-block read operations scored 14.09 GB/sec and writes registered 12.92 GB/sec, while PassMark database operations scored 997.36. Redis benchmark results reached 1.99 million SET operations per second, and static web serving delivered 3.65 GB/sec. Small 135M language model inference yields 211.8 prompt tokens per second and 59.25 generation tokens per second.

The ecs.g7t.large instance offers a cost-effective, low-concurrency option for foundational cloud architectures. Because of its limited multi-core capacity and reliance on remote storage, it is best suited for lightweight web serving, small microservices, edge proxies, utility tasks, and staging environments that benefit from balanced memory allocation without high sustained parallel compute demands.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7t.large is a general purpose instance in the Enhanced family featuring 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of memory on a 1:4 allocation ratio. Driven by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor with 1 physical core and 2 threads, it provides dedicated CPU resources, 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and relies fully on network storage with no local disks or GPUs bundled. In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits competent single-core metrics—scoring 1553.0 in Geekbench single-core and 28.03 GB/sec in gzip compression—but experiences noticeable throughput limits in multi-core metrics like stress-ng multi-core (1896.44) and software compilation due to its dual-vCPU count. The hardware setup delivers balanced, economical resource density suitable for lightweight web serving, non-critical background jobs, small backend services, and test workloads.
